newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. stocks seen with solid underpinning.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. stocks seen with solid underpinning.

text.p: A jump in the number of stocks hitting new highs, strength in financial shares and positive market breadth indicate U.S. stocks have a solid underpinning technical analysts said on Wednesday.
While stocks may pause and consolidate in the near-term, market internals are not flashing major warning signs of a sharp pullback ahead, the technicians said.
The Dow was off about 45 points at 7715 in late afternoon trading on Wednesday after posting small losses on Monday and Tuesday.
Last week the Dow capped a six-session run of record highs, closing Friday at 7782. That rally brought the Dow up almost 1,400 points, or 22 percent, from its 1997 low of 6392 on April 11.
"Markets don't go down just because they're up a lot," said Frank Gretz, technical analyst at Shields & Co.
"They go down when they start to lose participation, or people get too enthusiastic, or you get the Dow stocks going up and not the majority of stocks, and that hasn't happened," he added.
Last week 878 stocks on the New York Stock Exchange hit new highs.
Ken Tower, technical analyst at UST Securities, said its the most weekly new highs on the NYSE since the week of November 5, 1982.

In past bull markets, peaks in weekly new highs have led major market tops by an average of 34 weeks, said Joseph Barthel, director of investment strategy at Fahnestock, in a report citing Ned Davis Research.
The data "suggests that we should not be at a risk of recording a final bull market high until at least mid-February 1998," Barthel said.
Gretz also said the recent breakout by financial stocks was a further indication the market may not have peaked.
"Historically financial stocks usually peak several months before the overall market," he said.
Analysts said the breadth of the recent rally, with advancing issues soundly outnumbering decliners in recent sessions, is another bullish sign.
Tower said he was looking to buy on market dips on the view that they will not be extended.

"Even if (Friday's close) was the top, you're not going to have a serious decline for five or six months," he said. "The worst case scenario is you go flat. If that's your worst case scenario, then it's just a matter of being in the right stocks."
